title: After 1997, 28 saline Victorian streams became fresher and lost 6 points more salt than less rain explains, but saline baseflow carried only about one tenth of the lost runoff (2010-2021)
abstract: Question: after 1997, south-east Australian runoff stayed 20-25% below its 1951-1996 rainfall-runoff relation. Bore studies found falling water tables. Did the streams lose groundwater discharge, or other water? Approach: we used 34,318 stream electrical conductivity (EC) grab samples (Victorian WMIS) at 83 CAMELS-AUS v2.03 catchments as a groundwater tracer. We fitted EC-flow ratings for 1990-1996 and 2010-2022, computed daily salt flux, and split flow into saline baseflow and fresh quickflow with a two-component mass balance. Our null model is an effective-rain analogue: the rain decrease that gives the observed water loss in the pre-1997 model. A synthetic rain-decrease test and a 1981-1996 placebo gave no excess (-0.8 and -1.2 points). Results: at equal flow, EC fell 5.8% in all catchments, mostly at low flow (-10.7%; high flow -0.8%). In 28 saline catchments (groundwater EC at least 3 times flood EC), low-flow EC fell 19.5%; this developed in 1997-2009 and did not recover. Runoff was 30% below the rain relation; salt export fell 35%, against 27% for the analogue (excess -6.1 points, 95% CI -14.2 to -3.5). Baseflow fell 33% against 15% for the analogue if groundwater EC is fixed, but only 3 points beyond the analogue if groundwater became fresher. Saline baseflow carried 11% (-4 to 31%) of the lost water; at least about 70% was fresh quickflow, which fell as a 10% rain decrease predicts. Larger water-table shortfalls (23 catchments) went with more freshening-driven salt loss (rho 0.51). Six sensitivity runs agreed. Conclusion: less saline groundwater reached streams after 1997, but this loss is small in volume; groundwater discharge loss or stream-aquifer disconnection alone cannot explain the runoff deficit, which is mainly a smaller event-water response. Limitations: EC resolves the split only in the 28 saline, drier, cleared catchments; less versus fresher groundwater is not separable; monthly grab samples; the saline threshold was set after a first look; post hoc bore link.
